name: pi-eval discriminating suite
description: 41 tasks across 7 categories. Every predicate was verified against two answers before admission: a correct answer must PASS and a plausible-but-wrong answer must FAIL. A predicate that cannot fail a wrong answer turns a real difference into a tie, and ties carry no direction in the paired sign test — so a lax grader does not merely mismeasure, it destroys the suite's power. No category exceeds 15%: ten more tasks of one kind tend to pass and fail together and buy little additional discrimination.

tasks.prompt: In what year was the first working transistor built at Bell Labs? Answer with the year.
How many chromosomes are in a normal human somatic (body) cell? Answer with the number.
Which chemical element has atomic number 74? Answer with the element's name only, one word.
As of 2024, what is the capital city of Kazakhstan? Answer with only the city name, one word, no punctuation.
What is the specific term for the small reinforced tip at the end of a shoelace? Answer with the single word.
What is the name for the scholarly study of flags? Answer with the single word only, no punctuation.
What is the calendar date exactly 90 days after January 1, 2026? (2026 is not a leap year.) Respond with only the date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD, zero-padded), and nothing else.
List the five smallest prime numbers greater than 20, in ascending order. Respond with only the five numbers on a single line, separated by single commas with no spaces, and nothing else.

Convert the US phone number 1-800-555-0199 to E.164 format (a plus sign, then the country code followed by the ten-digit number, with no spaces, dashes, or parentheses). The US country code is 1. Respond with only the formatted number and nothing else.
Convert the time 12:05 AM to 24-hour clock format, zero-padded, using a colon separator (HH:MM). Respond with only the time and nothing else.

Convert the title  The Quick, Brown Fox!  into a URL slug: all lowercase, punctuation removed, words separated by single hyphens, with no leading or trailing hyphen. Respond with only the slug and nothing else.

Return ONLY a JSON object (no surrounding prose, no explanation) for an HTTP server configuration. It must have exactly these top-level keys: "host" (string), "port" (integer), "routes" (array of objects), and "tls" (an object with keys "enabled" and "cert_path"). Use host "0.0.0.0", port 443, one route object whose "path" is "/health" and "method" is "GET", and set tls enabled to true with cert_path "/etc/ssl/cert.pem".

Parse the string "name=Ada;role=admin;active=true" into JSON. Return ONLY a JSON object with a single top-level key "pairs" whose value is an array of objects, each object having exactly the keys "key" and "value". Keep every value as a string. Do not flatten the pairs into top-level keys.

Perform integer (floor) division of 100 by 7. Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: "dividend", "divisor", "quotient", and "remainder". Include the "remainder" key even though it may seem obvious. Use integer values, not a decimal quotient.

Given the UTC timestamp "2026-07-26T15:30:00Z", decompose it. Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: "year", "month", "day", "hour", "minute", "second", and "weekday". The numeric fields are integers; "weekday" is the full English day name for that date.

Transpose the 2x3 matrix [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]. Return ONLY a JSON object (not a bare array) with exactly these keys: "rows", "cols", and "transpose". "rows" and "cols" are the integer dimensions of the RESULT matrix, and "transpose" is the resulting nested array.

Solve the quadratic equation x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0. Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: "roots" (an array containing the two integer roots), "sum_of_roots", and "product_of_roots". No prose before or after the JSON.
Compute (17 × 23) − (144 ÷ 12). Reply with ONLY the resulting integer — digits only, with no words, no punctuation, no commas, and no explanation.
Is 91 a prime number? Reply with exactly one word — either YES or NO — in uppercase, with no punctuation and no other text.
Take this sentence: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Remove the word 'lazy'. Reply with the resulting sentence in all lowercase, with no punctuation of any kind and no extra words.
tasks.pattern: ^the quick brown fox jumps over the dog$

tasks.prompt: Reply with ONLY a JSON object of the form {"first": A, "second": B}, keeping the keys in that exact order, where A is the 5th prime number and B is the 8th prime number.

Name the four cardinal compass directions in clockwise order starting from north. Reply with exactly four words, all lowercase, separated by single spaces, with no commas, no punctuation, and nothing else.
Give the past tense of the English verb 'to dive'. Reply with a single lowercase word only, with no punctuation and no other text.

Order update: please keep your order confirmation code CNF-7X2Q9 handy — you'll be asked to quote it whenever you contact support. For our internal records your customer ID is CUST-40192, and the parcel's carrier tracking number is TRK-88213. Question: what is the customer ID? Respond with only the customer ID and nothing else.

Pricing page: the Basic plan is $9/month, the Pro plan is $29/month, and the Enterprise plan is $99/month. Right now the Pro plan is 50% off for the first three months. Question: what is the regular (non-discounted) monthly price of the Pro plan, in US dollars? Respond with just the number.

The agreement was signed on the 3rd of February, 2024. It becomes effective on March 1, 2024, and it expires exactly two years after the effective date. Question: give the EFFECTIVE date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Respond with only the date.

Contact directory: for sales inquiries, email sales@acme.example; for press and media, email press@acme.example; to file a formal complaint or escalate an unresolved issue, write to support-escalations@acme.example. authoring_notes: Computation tasks require a terminal 'ANSWER: <number>' line. Positional number extraction on free-form prose is not deterministic: a correct worked solution that ends '...which leaves 220 extra widgets' hands which="last" the number 220. Three of four apparent model failures in the first live run were this bug, not the models.

The two-answer admission gate verifies the PREDICATE, not the ANSWER KEY. notebooks-discount-tax shipped with expected=52.34 when the answer is 52.33, and the known-good answer I wrote to verify it contained the same arithmetic error — so the gate passed a self-consistently wrong task. Both models got it right and were marked wrong. Only a live run against a model that does its own arithmetic caught it.
